extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers/referees invited to review manuscripts for Scientific Reports (Nature Portfolio journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for referees on evaluating manuscripts submitted to Scientific Reports, covering publication criteria, specific evaluation questions (technical soundness, data, statistics, ethics), procedural expectations (confidentiality, timing, anonymity), AI use, and competing-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper must be scientifically valid and technically sound in methodology and analysis. Manuscripts are not assessed based on their perceived importance, significance or impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific Reports will publish niche scope work, work between disciplines, negative results, or scientifically-justified replications. The research community will judge importance after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Editorial Board Members with the information needed to reach a decision and instruct authors how to strengthen their manuscript to be acceptable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reviews on facts and actionable guidance that help editors decide and help authors improve technical soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment focus: technical soundness and scientific validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be mindful that they are assessing the manuscript on technical soundness and scientific validity — both methods and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must be appropriate and properly conducted, and the conclusions drawn must be fully supported by the data. Referees should not assess importance or significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the paper technically sound?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit question for reviewers to decide whether the study is technically correct and well-executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider study design, methodology, controls, reproducibility, and whether procedures were carried out correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the claims convincing?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the authors' claims are persuasive given the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not convincing, specify what further evidence or experiments are needed to support the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the claims fully supported by the experimental data?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the data presented in the manuscript fully back the stated conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify gaps between data and interpretation and request clarification or additional data where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether statistical analyses are appropriate, correctly performed, and correctly interpreted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check assumptions, sample sizes, error reporting, multiple comparisons corrections, and whether conclusions match statistical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the availability of data adhere to the expected standards of the research community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify data sharing, availability statements, repositories, and that data provided are sufficient to reproduce analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization with previous literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims appropriately discussed in the context of the previous literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness and balance of citations, whether prior work is acknowledged, and whether claims overstate novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript is unacceptable in its present form, determine whether the study seems sufficiently promising to encourage future resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise on whether major revisions/additional work could render the manuscript publishable and be specific about requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accessibility of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript clearly written? If not, how could it be made more accessible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear sections, recommend restructuring or clearer explanations, and suggest language edits if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns (animals/human subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any special ethical concerns arising from the use of animals or human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing ethics approval, consent issues, welfare concerns, or other ethical problems that could preclude publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps and institutional affiliation naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Reports remains strictly neutral with respect to jurisdictional claims in maps and institutional affiliations; naming conventions are left to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should not request changes to such naming conventions unless it is critical to the clarity of the scientific content.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on peer reviewers' use of generative AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools. If any part of the evaluation was supported by an AI tool, declare the use transparently in the peer review report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports review
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports are peer-reviewed prior to data collection and analyses to reduce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format minimizes publication and research bias while allowing exploratory analyses; referees invited to review Registered Reports should follow the journal's detailed Registered Reports guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board Members and reviewers must treat the review process as strictly confidential and not discuss the manuscript with anyone not directly involved in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to consult laboratory colleagues if they are identified to the Editorial Board Member. Consulting external experts requires checking with the Editorial Board Member to avoid involving excluded individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to provide a report promptly; ideally within 10 days of receiving a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a delay is anticipated, inform the Editorial Board Member and publishing office so authors can be kept informed and alternative referees found if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identities are not released to authors or other reviewers unless reviewers specifically ask to be identified; reviewers are preferred to remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should not identify themselves to authors without the Editorial Board Member's knowledge. If they wish to reveal their identities, this should be done via the publishing office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing of referees' reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not edit reviewer reports; comments intended for authors are transmitted as written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On rare occasions the journal may edit to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information. Reviewers are asked to avoid needless offence, but robust language does not imply unfairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests and conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should avoid reviewing when there are competing interests such as recent/ongoing collaborations, having commented on drafts, direct competition, a history of dispute, or financial interest in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should draw attention to anything that might affect their review and decline invitations if they feel unable to be objective. Editors recognize these situations are not always black-and-white and will weigh such factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-reviewing papers previously reviewed elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees who have reviewed a paper for another journal may still be asked to review it for Scientific Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that two journals independently identified the same referee does not by itself reduce the validity of their opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board Members select referees based on multiple factors, including expertise, specific recommendations, and previous experience; reviewer invitations are confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection aims to choose appropriate expert referees; reviewers should expect confidentiality of the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to provide follow-up advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are requested to be willing to provide follow-up advice upon resubmission when asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Board Members may not re-send resubmitted papers to referees if authors have not made a serious attempt to address criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online manuscript review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees must submit their comments via the journal's online submission system using the link in the invitation email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For help with the manuscript tracking system, contact the journal's support team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering reviewer reports, the Editorial Board Member will make one of: Accept outright; Request a minor revision; Request a major revision; Reject outright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor revision = authors revise to address specific concerns. Major revision = significant concerns and perhaps additional work. Editors may seek original reviewers' advice after resubmission.
